newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Delayed IMF funding pressures Bulgarian lev.
newsitem.headline: Delayed IMF funding pressures Bulgarian lev.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev weakened to 222-223 per dollar at the close from 215 in the morning as foreign currency demand rose due to concerns over delayed International Monetary Fund (IMF) funding, dealers said.
"Traders fear that the lev may fall sharply after the International Monetary Fund again postponed the second (funding) tranche," a dealer said.

Bulgaria's Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Saturday the IMF has postponed a second $115 million tranche of funding until Bulgaria completes reform pledges and its stabilisation measures show results.

Uncertainty whether Bulgaria will meet the reform targets quickly enough to qualify for the IMF funding boosted foreign currency demand on the local interbank market amid shrinking supply, the dealer added.

The central bank was reported to have launched dollar sales after the lev fell beyond 220 per dollar in the early afternoon but volumes seemed to be insufficient to meet dollar demand and support the lev, dealers said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.

The lev's fall today was in sharp contrast with its rise over the past two weeks after a record high main interest rate of 300 percent came into effect and banks pared forex positions to profit from high yield lev-denominated investments.
"The high interest rate combined with hopes of an imminent IMF funding to support the lev, but now it seems the (lev's) rise is over," another dealer said.
The lev traded at 236-237 per dollar just before the rate hike was announced on September 23. @

The advance of the lev to 209-210 per dollar on Friday from 220 at the opening was not realistic and now it was normal for the dollar to rebound, dealers said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
